To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

brief assessments can be used to identify the presence of a functional relationship between a target behavior and a putative reinforcer, and extended analyses can be used to clarify and refine those results.
the sequence of assessments described here may be used as an effective tool to evaluate aberrant behavior.
the assessment of severe behavior problems can be conducted in an orderly and efficient manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of assessment that moves through four progressive phases.
the role of extended experimental analyses in providing a basis for the development of treatment programs.
the development of an experimental assessment strategy that is sensitive to the needs of the clinician.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
17 of 20 (85%) participants showed clear and replicable responses to experimental manipulations.
for 85% (17 of 20) of participants, a functional relation was established.
85% of participants exhibited aberrant behavior that responded to experimental manipulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model is effective in guiding treatment, but that it is not always successful in identifying clear and replicable patterns.
the model was successful in guiding the selection of effective treatments for 85% and 15% of the participants, respectively.
the model described here is useful in identifying and controlling for confounding effects in the assessment of severe behavior problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

brief assessments are often not enough to understand aberrant behavior and that a sequence of increasingly extended experimental analyses can provide a more complete understanding of aberrant behavior.
the assessment sequence described here can be used to identify the variables that control behavior in a manner that is consistent with experimental principles.
extended experimental analyses are often necessary to identify the function of aberrant behaviors.
